title: DevEx is for Humans, AX is for Agents: Measuring Context Health in Agentic Software Work
abstract: arXiv:2611.33480v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Coding agents succeed or fail in the context humans give them, yet most evaluations measure only output. Drawing on developer experience research, we introduce Agent Experience (AX), an instrument that scores session transcripts on four dimensions of the CAFE(S) framework: Clarity, Actionability, Fidelity, and Efficiency; Security, a gate rather than a friction dimension, is out of scope. A rubric-guided language model rates each dimension from 1 to 5 and explains what the human could have provided. We report on three studies that tested this model. In the Stack Overflow Developer Survey, respondents reporting context problems were less likely to rate AI as very useful in all seven activities examined (12-28%). Across 882 rated agentic sessions from a pilot sample of 1,000, Actionability received the lowest ratings (59.6% of ratings at or below 3, versus 26.6% for Fidelity), and ratings were lower in longer sessions. translated_title: DevEx 面向人类，AX 面向智能体：度量智能体软件工作中的上下文健康度
translated_abstract: 编码智能体的成败取决于人类所提供的上下文，然而大多数评估只衡量输出结果。借鉴开发者体验研究成果，我们提出了智能体体验（AX），这是一种对会话记录在 CAFE(S) 框架的四个维度上进行评分的工具：清晰度、可操作性、保真度和效率；安全性作为门槛而非摩擦维度，不在本工具的评估范围内。一个由评分标准引导的语言模型对每个维度进行 1 到 5 分的评分，并解释人类本可以提供哪些内容。我们报告了三项检验该模型的研究。在 Stack Overflow 开发者调查中，报告存在上下文问题的受访者在所考察的全部七项活动中都更不可能认为 AI 非常有用（降幅为 12-28%）。在对 1,000 个试点样本中的 882 个智能体会话进行评分后，可操作性获得的评分最低（59.6% 的评分为 3 分或以下，而保真度仅为 26.6%），且会话越长评分越低。
tldr: 该论文提出智能体体验（AX）框架，通过从清晰度、可操作性、保真度和效率四个维度对智能体会话中的上下文质量进行评分，揭示人类提供的上下文质量（尤其是可操作性）是决定编码智能体成败的关键因素。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Agent Experience (AX), a framework that scores the quality of context provided to coding agents across four dimensions—Clarity, Actionability, Fidelity, and Efficiency—revealing that the context health of human input, especially Actionability, is a key determinant of agentic success.
